chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Minqari from whom he mentioned, saying:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who divorces his wife while they have a child, which of them has more right to the child? He said, 'The wife has more right to the child as long as she has not married.'

This report does not contradict what we previously mentioned that the father is more entitled to the child, because we interpret this report as meaning that if the wife undertakes the care of her child with the same provision the father gives for another, then she, in that state, is more entitled to him as we mentioned. It is also possible that what is meant by 'child' here is if the child is female, for the mother is more entitled to her as long as she has not married. It is not in this report that she is more entitled before the two years and weaning or after it, and we have clarified that she is more entitled as long as she is not weaned according to the condition we mentioned. And if that is not explicit in its text, we interpret it as meaning she is more entitled before weaning.
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And upon the father, after the child reaches two years, is not the wage of breastfeeding.
ai.seo_question: Who has more right to the child after divorce according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent tension between this narration and the father's primary right by interpreting the Imam's statement as conditional upon the mother receiving equivalent financial support or applying specifically to female children. This scholarly reconciliation highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence where maternal custody is prioritized during the nursing period (before weaning) provided she remains unmarried, while acknowledging that the father's obligation for nursing compensation ceases once the child reaches two years of age. The text thus establishes a flexible framework balancing maternal nurturing rights with paternal financial responsibilities within the context of divorce.
